subject.title: fix(agents): make model-facing tool schemas llama.cpp GBNF-compatible (#108580)

question: Should llama.cpp incompatibilities be handled by globally removing constraints from canonical model-facing schemas, or by provider/profile-specific normalization that preserves them for other providers?
rationale: The global approach fixes otherwise-undetectable custom llama.cpp endpoints automatically but weakens schema-constrained generation for every provider; the provider-boundary approach preserves existing contracts but needs an explicit and discoverable path for custom endpoints.

options.title: Use provider projection
options.body: Restore canonical constraints and strip incompatible keywords only for recognized llama.cpp providers or an explicit profile, with proof for both projected and ordinary-provider schemas.

options.title: Accept global weakening
options.body: Land this branch with an explicit maintainer decision that model-facing schemas should enforce structure only and all affected size limits should be runtime-owned.

options.title: Pause for the competing branch
options.body: Wait for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/108469 to become clean, narrowly scoped, and proof-positive before choosing it as the canonical implementation.

recommendation.title: Use provider projection
recommendation.body: Restore canonical constraints and strip incompatible keywords only for recognized llama.cpp providers or an explicit profile, with proof for both projected and ordinary-provider schemas.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history connects this person to both the cron schema and provider-normalization boundaries involved in the decision.
